key_insight: For jointly supervised ResNets, the authors prove a turnpike property: the number of layers needed to reach a prescribed loss level is bounded independently of total network depth.
engineering_relevance: The theory helps explain why early exits can reduce inference computation and why networks of different depths can show similar early-exit performance.
method: Model ResNet propagation and joint intermediate/output loss optimization using optimal control theory.
Prove a turnpike property and derive similarity implications for internal representations across network depths.
Connect turnpikes to overthinking and analyze entropy- and maximum-probability-based exit criteria.
evidence_signal: Experiments demonstrate turnpike behavior and similar early-exit performance across ResNets of varying depths; the abstract provides no datasets or quantitative results.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify the theorem’s assumptions, so its depth-independent guarantee should not be assumed to cover arbitrary architectures or training setups.
paper_title: Towards an Optimal Control Foundation of Early Exits - Turnpikes and ResNets
